div.b: The host owns the real resources

div.span: - One physical server with a processor, memory, a network card and some storage. On its own it serves one operating system at a time.

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #FFFFFF;

div.b: The hypervisor cuts them into shares

div.span: - It is the software that virtualizes the host. The processor becomes vCPUs, the memory becomes vRAM, the network card becomes vNICs.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 38px; height: 1px; padding-top: 391px; margin-left: 1206px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #FFFFFF;

div.b: Each machine gets its own share

div.span: - It boots its own operating system and sees only its slice. Machines are added until the host is full, and none of them can read its neighbours.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 38px; height: 1px; padding-top: 561px; margin-left: 1206px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #FFFFFF;

div.b: Storage route one: over the network

div.span: - The volume lives elsewhere and reaches the host over the network; the hypervisor hands it to the machine as a plain disk. This is the EBS volume in Task 4, and it survives a stop.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 38px; height: 1px; padding-top: 731px; margin-left: 1206px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #FFFFFF;

div.b: Storage route two: a disk in the host

div.span: - The hypervisor passes through a disk physically inside the server. Nothing crosses the network, so it is the fastest route, and it is also the one you lose when the instance stops.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 38px; height: 1px; padding-top: 901px; margin-left: 1206px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #FFFFFF;
display: inline-block; font-size: 22px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#FFFFFF, #121212); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 546px; height: 1px; padding-top: 883px; margin-left: 1259px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 14px; font-family: Helvetica; color: var(--ge-adaptive-fg, #000000); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.b: Storage route three: around the hypervisor

div.span: - A shared file system is mounted over the virtual network card, so the hypervisor never takes part. Many machines can read the same files at once. On AWS, EFS or FSx.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 578px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1033px; margin-left: 1223px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: var(--ge-adaptive-fg, #000000); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.span: - Type 1 sits straight on the hardware. Fewer layers means lower latency and less to attack, which is why providers use it. The instance in this lab runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, a type 1 built on KVM.
- Type 2 runs as an application on a desktop operating system. The extra layer costs latency, which is acceptable on a laptop but not in a data centre.
- Without a hypervisor, one box serves one tenant. With one, the same box serves many isolated machines: that is multitenancy, and it is what makes renting compute cheap.
- The instance type you pick in Task 4, t3.micro, names the size of the slice: how much vCPU and vRAM the hypervisor hands your machine.
- Storage is the one resource the hypervisor does not always mediate, which is why the three routes above behave so differently when an instance is stopped.

a.text: Text is not SVG - cannot display
